thread:
javier: Heads-up — prod Docusaurus build failed on main with a bunch of broken fragment links. Looks like many anchors were generated with invisible ZWSP characters inside the slug.

linter-bot: linkcheck: broken link detected — /docs/getting-started#quickstart -> fragment not found (actual id: #quickstart​)

javier: The root cause seems to be copy/paste from some third-party examples where a ZWSP (U+200B) sneaks into headings inside fenced code blocks, and the slugifier includes it. Locally the site scrolls but the static linkcheck treats them as different.

robin: Yikes. Two clean options: 1) run a one-off migration to strip ZWSPs from markdown sources, 2) add explicit HTML anchors next to problematic headings (`<a id="quickstart" />`) as a short-term fix.

elaine: I'd prefer a combined approach: quick content patch for top pages + committed normalization step to prevent regressions. We should also add a unit test to the docs pipeline to assert no source files contain ​.

javier: Agreed. I'll draft a small Node script we can run in CI and as a pre-commit hook. Example: 
```
// strip-zwsp.js (toy)
const fs = require('fs')
for (const f of process.argv.slice(2)) {
  const s = fs.readFileSync(f, 'utf8')
  const cleaned = s.replace(/\u200B/g, '')
  fs.writeFileSync(f, cleaned)
}
```
We can wire this into `package.json` as `precommit` and add a docs CI check.

robin: For the short term I'll open a docs PR that adds explicit anchors to about 6 high-traffic pages (getting-started, quickstart, sdk-usage). We'll mark them with an HTML comment explaining it's a temporary fallback. Use `aria-hidden="true"`.

elaine: Please also include a mention in the PR description that this is a temporary workaround and link the migration script/issue. Keeps reviewer context.

javier: I'll also add a `linkcheck.ignore` rule to skip fragments that match `.*\u200B` until we merge the fixes, to avoid blocking releases. But that will be very temporary.

robin: PRs: docs patch https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/1901, strip script + precommit https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/1902 (both opened).

docs-bot: CI status: docs PR #1901 — checks running.

linter-bot: Pre-check suggestion: add a test to `tests/docs/test_no_zwsp.py` asserting `\u200B` not in any `.md` or `.mdx`. Example: `assert not any('\u200B' in open(f).read() for f in md_files)`

elaine: Good call. @robin please include that test in PR #1902. Also squash the content patch into a single commit so we can revert the fallback anchors easily.

robin: Will do. Assigning reviewers: @elaine on content patch, @javier on strip script.

javier: Once #1902 lands I'll trigger a docs rebuild on staging and run the linkcheck. If all good we'll merge both and then remove the linkcheck ignore.

docs-bot: /retest requested after PR merges.

elaine: Quick QA note — when you add anchors, test the anchors in mobile Safari and Chrome. We saw slight scroll-offset differences previously.

robin: Noted — I'll add manual QA steps in the PR description and ping QA when staging is up.

javier: Plan recap: 1) short-term content anchors on key pages (PR 1901), 2) strip-zwsp precommit + CI test (PR 1902), 3) run migration script across repo, 4) remove fallback anchors in cleanup PR once migration validated.

elaine: Sounds good. Thanks for moving fast on this — weird invisible chars are the worst. :grimacing:

robin: Done for now. I'll post updates as the PRs progress. :rocket:
